name: stonecut-blockbench-mcp

tools.name: ping
tools.description: Checks that Blockbench is open, the Stonecut Bridge plugin is listening and the token is right. Returns the plugin version.

tools.name: status
tools.description: Whether the GeckoLib plugin is installed, the allowed folders (output, assets), the open project (format, bones, cubes, textures, animations, and for Java models the display transforms) and every open tab with its edit count. Call this first.

tools.name: new_project
tools.description: Opens a new tab with an empty GeckoLib animated entity model (a Bedrock entity model if the GeckoLib Blockbench plugin is missing; the reply then has a warning). 16 units = 1 block; the model stands on y=0 and faces north (-Z).

name.description: Model name, also the geometry name.

texture_height.description: Texture UV height. Default the width.

modid.description: Mod id stored in the GeckoLib project settings.

tools.name: open_model
tools.description: Opens an existing Bedrock/GeckoLib .geo.json in a new tab (converted to GeckoLib format when that plugin is installed), optionally with its .animation.json and texture PNG. If the file is already open it switches to that tab instead.

geo.description: Absolute path, or "output:<relative path>" / "assets:<relative path>". Must end with .json.

animation.description: Absolute path, or "output:<relative path>" / "assets:<relative path>". Must end with .json.

texture.description: Absolute path, or "output:<relative path>" / "assets:<relative path>". Must end with .png.

reopen.description: Open a new tab even if this file is already open.

reload.description: If the file is already open with no edits, close that tab and load the file again.

tools.name: close_tab
tools.description: Closes extra copies of a tab, keeping the first. A copy is closed only when it matches the kept tab (name, format, element and texture count) and has no edits, so no work is lost.

name.description: Tab name whose duplicates to close.

duplicates.description: true: close duplicates of every tab.

tools.name: add_bones
tools.description: Adds bones (groups). Only bones animate, so every GeckoLib cube goes in a bone. Start with one root bone, then body, head, legs... with pivots where the joints are. Names must be unique. Nothing is created if any entry is bad.

parent.description: An existing bone, or one earlier in this list.

pivot.description: Joint position [x, y, z]; the bone rotates around it. Default [0, 0, 0].

tools.name: add_cubes
tools.description: Adds cubes. Give "from"+"to" or "origin"+"size". GeckoLib models use box UV: give each cube its own uv_offset so UV islands do not overlap. Java models may use "faces" for per-face UVs and need no bone. Nothing is created if any entry is bad.

bone.description: Bone to put the cube in. Required for GeckoLib models; Java models may leave it out.

origin.description: Min corner in Blockbench coordinates. Use with "size".

uv_offset.description: Box UV offset [u, v]. A cube of size w,h,d needs a 2*(w+d) by (d+h) area.

pivot.description: Rotation point. Default: the bone pivot, or the cube centre.

additionalProperties.description: [u1, v1, u2, v2] in texture pixels, or {uv, rotation}, or null to remove the face.

tools.name: texture_create
tools.description: Creates the project texture, or resizes it (the canvas grows or shrinks and old pixels stay at the top-left). Also sets the project UV size unless set_uv_size is false.

name.description: Texture name for a new texture, for example "sword.png".

keep_pixels.description: Keep the old pixels when resizing. Default true.

set_uv_size.description: Also set the project UV size. Default true.

tools.name: texture_fill_rect
tools.description: Fills a rectangle of the texture with one colour (or clears it).

tools.name: texture_set_pixels
tools.description: Sets single pixels: a list of [x, y, colour].

tools.name: texture_draw
tools.description: Draws a small picture from rows of characters, for example rows ["..ab..", ".abba."] with palette {"a": "#ff0000", "b": "#000000"}. Characters not in the palette are skipped. Each character covers scale x scale pixels.

tools.name: texture_import
tools.description: Loads a PNG from the output or assets folder as the project texture.

path.description: Absolute path, or "output:<relative path>" / "assets:<relative path>". Must end with .png.

set_uv_size.description: Set the project UV size to the image size. Default false.

tools.name: add_animation
tools.description: Adds an animation, for example idle, walk or attack. Looping animations should end on the pose they start with.

length.description: Seconds. Default 1. Grows to fit later keyframes.

tools.name: add_keyframes
tools.description: Adds keyframe tracks to an animation: per bone and channel (rotation in degrees, position in units, scale as factors).

value.description: [x, y, z] numbers or Molang strings, or one number for all three.

interpolation.description: Default for every keyframe. Default linear.

tools.name: screenshot
tools.description: Renders the 3D preview from named views (or yaw/pitch in degrees) and returns the images; PNG files are also written to the output folder. The camera frames the model and is put back afterwards. "right" is the model's right side when it faces north. Give animation + time to see a pose. Screenshot often and check every side.

yaw.description: Custom camera yaw in degrees, used when no view is given. 0 looks at the front.

pitch.description: Custom camera pitch in degrees. Default 15.

distance.description: Camera distance. Default fits the model.

path.description: File for a single view. Default an automatic name in the output folder.

overwrite.description: Replace files that already exist. Default false.

tools.name: export
tools.description: Writes the open project: geo (.geo.json, GeckoLib/Bedrock), animation (.animation.json with all animations), model (Java block/item .json with its display block, Java projects only) and texture (.png). Existing files are kept unless overwrite is true.

geo.description: Absolute path, or "output:<relative path>" / "assets:<relative path>". Must end with .geo.json.

animation.description: Absolute path, or "output:<relative path>" / "assets:<relative path>". Must end with .animation.json.

model.description: Absolute path, or "output:<relative path>" / "assets:<relative path>". Must end with .json.

texture.description: Absolute path, or "output:<relative path>" / "assets:<relative path>". Must end with .png.

overwrite.description: Replace files that already exist. Default false.

tools.name: open_java_model
tools.description: Opens a Java block/item model .json that has "elements" in a new tab. Its texture comes from "texture", a same-named PNG next to the model, or assets/textures/...; anything else shows blank. Parent models are not followed. If the file is already open it switches to that tab.

model.description: Absolute path, or "output:<relative path>" / "assets:<relative path>". Must end with .json.

texture.description: Absolute path, or "output:<relative path>" / "assets:<relative path>". Must end with .png.

name.description: Tab name. Default the file name.

reopen.description: Open a new tab even if this file is already open.

reload.description: If the file is already open with no edits, close that tab and load the file again.

tools.name: new_java_item
tools.description: Opens a new tab with an empty Java block/item model, for example a weapon. Cubes need no bones. Optional display transforms, given directly or copied from a preset file.

namespace.description: Namespace for texture links, as in "<namespace>:item/<name>". Default minecraft.

scale.description: [x, y, z], each within -4..4. Negative mirrors.

preset.description: A .json file with a "display" block (for example another item model) in the output or assets folder.

tools.name: display_get
tools.description: The display transforms of the open Java model: every set slot, or one slot.

tools.name: display_set
tools.description: Sets display transforms (undoable). Give "display" for several slots, or "slot" with rotation/translation/scale, or a "preset" file. Fields you leave out keep their value unless replace is true.

scale.description: [x, y, z], each within -4..4. Negative mirrors.
[x, y, z], each within -4..4. Negative mirrors.

preset.description: A .json file with a "display" block (for example another item model) in the output or assets folder.

replace.description: Reset each given slot before applying. Default false.

tools.name: display_screenshot
tools.description: Renders display slots as the Blockbench display editor shows them and returns the images (PNG files also go to the output folder). First person is uncropped by default so you see how much of the view the item takes; gui is the inventory square.

overwrite.description: Replace files that already exist. Default false.

instructions:
Stonecut Blockbench MCP drives the Blockbench desktop app through the Stonecut Bridge plugin.

Files: paths are absolute, or start with "output:" (the output folder) or "assets:" (the optional assets folder). Nothing outside those two folders can be read or written. Call status to see them.

Settings: the person controls a settings file (status shows it): whether export is allowed, size limits for textures, files and cube count, and when Blockbench asks them to confirm (by default before replacing a file or closing a tab). If a call is refused because of it, tell the person which setting refused it and stop; do not try to get around it.

GeckoLib mob:
1. status, then new_project (64x64 texture for small mobs, 128 for large) or open_model.
2. Bones first: one root bone, then body, head, legs... with pivots at the joints. 16 units = 1 block; the model stands on y=0 and faces north (-Z).
3. Cubes next with add_cubes: block out big shapes, screenshot (views front, right, iso), fix proportions, then add detail. Give each cube its own uv_offset.
4. Texture: texture_create, texture_fill_rect per UV island, then texture_draw / texture_set_pixels for eyes, shading and edges.
5. Animate: add_animation, add_keyframes. Screenshot at a few times.
6. export geo, animation and texture when it looks right.

Java item (for example a sword):
1. new_java_item (optionally with display transforms or a preset), add_cubes without bones, texture_create, texture_draw.
2. display_screenshot with slots firstperson_righthand, thirdperson_righthand, gui. Tune with display_set and shoot again.
3. export model and texture.

Leave tabs open for the user; never close a tab with edits.
